title: Cap. 6 Arg. 7 open: If grace is fixed for all who apply Christ, the last reason falls to human choice
pass_a_gloss: If the will of God by the death of Christ is understood as quasi-determined to administering grace to all and each human beings who apply Christ to themselves and are saved, yet so that those alone receive and have it who either have used the light of nature well, or have least opposed an obstacle to the grace offered to them, while all the rest do not receive the same; then the last reason of grace and of salvation obtained and not obtained would be assigned not from the side of the divine good pleasure, but from the side of human free choice. The consequence is clear and firm; because by those who are established in this opinion, God is presumed, on account of the death of Christ, to administer grace and to offer to all a grace sufficient for applying Christ to themselves and obtaining salvation; he is also presumed, from absolute will or from bare will, to give saving grace to no one.
pass_b_english: Suppose God's will, by Christ's death, is taken as somehow fixed to administer grace to every person who applies Christ to himself and is saved—yet so that only those receive and keep it who either used nature's light well, or raised almost no obstacle against the grace offered them, while everyone else does not receive it. Then the last account of grace obtained or missed, and of salvation gained or lost, would be charged not to the divine good pleasure but to human free choice. The consequence is plain and solid. On that view God is presumed, because of Christ's death, to administer grace and to offer everyone a grace sufficient for applying Christ and obtaining salvation; and he is also presumed, by absolute will or bare will, to give saving grace to no one specially.
source_text: Si Dei voluntas morte Christi intelligatur quasi determinata ad gratiam administrandam omnibus & singulis hominibus, qui Christum sibi applicent, & salventur, ita tamen ut eam accipiant & habeant illi soli, qui aut lumine naturae bene usi fuerint, aut gratiae sibi oblatae obicem minime opposuerint, caeteri omnes eandem non accipiant; tum ultima ratio gratiae & salutis obtentae & non obtentae non ex parte Divini beneplaciti, sed ex parte humani arbitrii assignaretur. Consequentia clara est & firma; Quia ab illis qui in hac opinione constituti sunt, Deus praesumitur propter Christi mortem gratiam administrare, & offerre omnibus sufficientem ad Christum sibi applicandum & salutem obtinendam; praesumitur etiam ex absoluta voluntate sive ex mero nemini gratiam salutiferam donare.
